1-1.title: Math is Mine
1-1.contentObjective: I can describe the ways we are all doers of math, and compare my math story with a classmate's.
1-1.languageObjective: I can tell my math story using the words strength, challenge, and I use math when ___ .

vocabulary.definition: Anyone who uses mathematical thinking — which is everyone, every day.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquiera que use el pensamiento matemático, es decir, todos, todos los días.
vocabulary.visual: Splitting a bill 4 ways at dinner — that is a doer of math.

vocabulary.definition: Your own history with mathematics — what you have done, felt, and learned so far.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tu propia historia con las matemáticas: lo que has hecho, sentido y aprendido.
vocabulary.visual: “In 3rd grade I hated fractions; this year I can explain them.”

vocabulary.definition: Something you already do well and can share with others.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que ya haces bien y puedes compartir con otros.
vocabulary.visual: “I am good at mental math with money” — a strength you can teach.

vocabulary.definition: To break a number into parts that add, subtract, multiply, or divide back to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un número en partes que se combinan para volver a formarlo.
vocabulary.visual: 78.5 = 70 + 8.5, and also 157 ÷ 2 — both rebuild the same number.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, without counting every one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin contar todo.
vocabulary.visual: 20 cars × about 4 riders ≈ 80 people on the Ferris wheel.

1-1.workedExample:
The Ferris wheel has 20 cars, and about 4 people fit in each car. About how many people can ride at one time?
I count the cars: 20. Then I estimate how many riders fit in one car: about 4.
I do not count every person — an estimate is a reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful.
20 × 4 = 80, so I would say “about 80 people.”

1-2.contentObjective: I can make sense of a problem, plan a strategy, and use fractions of a whole number to compare quantities.

vocabulary.definition: An amount in a problem — a number with a meaning attached, like 540 meters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad en un problema: un número con un significado, como 540 metros.
vocabulary.visual: 540 meters — the number 540 AND what it measures.

vocabulary.definition: How two quantities compare or connect to each other.

vocabulary.visual: 1 hour → 48 km, 2 hours → 96 km: as one grows, so does the other.

vocabulary.definition: A plan for how to solve a problem before you start computing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un plan para resolver un problema antes de empezar a calcular.
vocabulary.visual: “I will draw a tape diagram first, then divide” — chosen before computing.

vocabulary.definition: A solution that makes sense in the context of the problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una solución que tiene sentido en el contexto del problema.

vocabulary.definition: To keep working on a problem, checking your progress and adjusting your plan when you get stuck.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Seguir trabajando en un problema, revisando tu progreso y ajustando tu plan cuando te atascas.
vocabulary.visual: Stuck on the tram problem → try a tape diagram instead → keep going.

1-2.workedExample:
A bowl is full of peas — far too many to count one at a time. About how many peas are in the bowl?
I do not count every pea — I look for a group I CAN count, like one small cluster of about 10.
Then I ask how many of those clusters would cover the whole bowl. I count about 12.
12 clusters of about 10 is 12 × 10 = 120, so my estimate is about 120 peas — a reasoned answer, close enough to be useful.

1-4.title: Math is Explaining and Sharing
1-4.contentObjective: I can construct an argument using equations, drawings, or words, and use volume to defend a recommendation.
1-4.languageObjective: I can explain my thinking with clear math vocabulary using the words argument, conjecture, and cubic units.

vocabulary.definition: A chain of reasons — equations, drawings, or words — used to defend your thinking.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cadena de razones — ecuaciones, dibujos o palabras — que usas para defender tu pensamiento.
vocabulary.visual: “Two jumbo boxes hold more, because 400 × 2 = 800 > 720.”

vocabulary.definition: A mathematical statement you believe is true but have not yet proven.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una afirmación matemática que crees verdadera pero que aún no has probado.
vocabulary.visual: “A bigger box ALWAYS holds more cereal” — believed, not yet proven.

vocabulary.definition: A single example that shows a statement is not always true.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo ejemplo que muestra que una afirmación no siempre es verdadera.
vocabulary.visual: One jumbo box sold half full of air breaks “bigger always holds more”.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of space a solid figure takes up, measured in cubic units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio que ocupa una figura sólida, medida en unidades cúbicas.
vocabulary.visual: 8 in × 3 in × 10 in = 240 cubic inches of cereal space.

vocabulary.definition: A cube with edges 1 unit long — the unit used to measure volume.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un cubo cuyas aristas miden 1 unidad — la unidad que se usa para medir el volumen.
vocabulary.visual: One cube, 1 unit on every edge — the block volume is counted in.

1-4.workedExample:
Suppose each large box is 8 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. Its volume is 8 × 3 × 10 = 240 cubic inches, so three large boxes hold 240 × 3 = 720 cubic inches.
Suppose each jumbo box is 10 inches long, 4 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. Its volume is 10 × 4 × 10 = 400 cubic inches, so two jumbo boxes hold 400 × 2 = 800 cubic inches.
I recommend buying two jumbo boxes because 800 cubic inches is greater than 720 cubic inches — the total volume is greater, so there is more cereal for the same price.

1-5.title: Math is Finding Patterns
1-5.contentObjective: I can find patterns and pattern rules, use them to make generalizations, and check my solutions with a table of values.

vocabulary.definition: Something that repeats or changes in a predictable way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que se repite o cambia de una manera predecible.
vocabulary.visual: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31 — each tower's steps follow a predictable jump.

vocabulary.definition: The instruction that tells how to get from one number in a pattern to the next.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La instrucción que dice cómo pasar de un número del patrón al siguiente.
vocabulary.visual: 2, 4, 6, 8 … the rule is “+ 2 every time”.

vocabulary.definition: A statement that is true for a whole pattern, made by noticing repeated calculations.

vocabulary.definition: A table that lists each step of a pattern so you can check that a solution is reasonable.

vocabulary.definition: Whether an answer makes sense — checked as you work, with adjustments made when needed.

1-5.workedExample:
A change jar is full of pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters worth $53.50 in total. How many of each coin could there be?
Each penny has a value of $0.01, so 100 pennies have a value of $1.00.
Each nickel has a value of $0.05, so 100 nickels have a value of $5.00. Each dime has a value of $0.10, so 100 dimes have a value of $10. Each quarter has a value of $0.25, so 100 quarters have a value of $25.
I multiply the number of each coin by its value. And I notice a generalization: because the jar's total, $53.50, ends in 0, the number of pennies can only be a multiple of 5.

vocabulary.definition: A way of showing a problem — a drawing, table, equation, or model — that helps you see it.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of attack for a problem — and something you can switch when you get stuck.

vocabulary.definition: To examine an idea and say what is convincing or not — about the idea, never about the person.

vocabulary.definition: A rule the whole class agrees to so that everyone can learn together.

1-6.workedExample:
First I make sense of it: one rack holds 8 bikes, each bike has 2 wheels, so this rack has 8 × 2 = 16 wheels. The other rack has 6 times as many wheels — that is what I don't know yet.
I choose a representation: 6 equal groups of 16. Then I make a plan: multiply.
16 × 6 = 96, so the other rack has about 96 wheels. I check my progress: 96 is 6 groups of 16, and 16 × 6 = 96, so my answer matches my plan.

2-1.title: Understand Statistical Questions
2-1.contentObjective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.
2-1.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words statistical question, data, variability, and survey.

vocabulary.definition: A statistical question expects varied answers that can be collected as data.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta estadística espera respuestas variadas que se pueden recopilar como datos.
vocabulary.visual: How many minutes do students in our class read each night?

vocabulary.definition: A question where the answers will be different for different people.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta cuyas respuestas serán distintas para distintas personas.
vocabulary.visual: “How tall are the players on the team?” → answers vary: 60 in, 63 in, 58 in, 65 in

vocabulary.definition: A question that has just one fixed answer that is the same no matter who you ask, so there is no data to collect.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta que tiene una sola respuesta fija, igual sin importar a quién le preguntes, por lo que no hay datos que recolectar.
vocabulary.visual: “How tall am I?” → one answer: 60 in. Everyone who measures gets the same number.

vocabulary.definition: Facts and numbers you collect, like answers to a survey.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Datos y números que recoges, como respuestas a una encuesta.
vocabulary.visual: Player heights: 60 in, 63 in, 58 in, 65 in — four different measurements

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: Scores 10, 12, 11 are close together (low variability); scores 2, 15, 30 are far apart (high variability)

vocabulary.definition: Collecting facts by asking people questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Recoger datos haciendo preguntas a las personas.
vocabulary.visual: Asking 50 students 'What is your favorite sport?' and recording the answers

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: If most scores cluster in the middle with fewer at the edges, the distribution is symmetric

2-1.workedExample:
Question 1: "How many points did our top player score last night?" There is one player and one game, so there is one fixed answer, like 18 points.
One answer, no variety, so this is NOT a statistical question.
Question 2: "How many points does each player score per game?" The answers vary: 8, 12, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22.
Because the answers are different for different players, I must collect data. This IS a statistical question.

vocabulary.term: Describe the Data Using the Median
vocabulary.termEs: Describir los datos con la mediana
vocabulary.definition: Using the middle value of the ordered data to say what is typical for the whole set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar el valor del medio de los datos ordenados para decir qué es típico en todo el conjunto.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 → the middle (3rd) value is 5, so median = 5

vocabulary.definition: The number that shows up most often.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que aparece más veces.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7 → 3 appears twice (most often), so mode = 3

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 10, 12, 11, 13, 50 → 50 is far from the others, so 50 is an outlier

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: If most values cluster in the center with fewer at the ends, the distribution is symmetric

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: 8, 9, 10, 11 has low variability (close together); 2, 10, 25, 40 has high variability (far apart)

2-3.workedExample:
My data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9 — five values, already in order. Ordering first is what makes a middle exist at all.
With 5 values, the middle is the 3rd one. Counting in from both ends: 2 and 9 pair off, 4 and 6 pair off, and 4 is left alone.
So the median is 4. Half the values sit at or below it and half at or above it.
Now an even set: 2, 4, 6, 9. There is no single middle, so I take the mean of the two middle values: (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5. The median is 5, even though 5 is not in the data.

vocabulary.termEs: Representar datos con diagramas de caja

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers that split the data into four equal parts.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.

2-5.title: Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range
2-5.contentObjective: I can find the range and the interquartile range of a data set and use them to describe how spread out the data is.
2-5.languageObjective: I can explain what the spread of a data set is using the words range, quartile, interquartile range, and vary.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers that describe spread: the range covers all the data, and the interquartile range covers only the middle half.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números que describen la dispersión: el rango cubre todos los datos y el rango intercuartílico solo la mitad central.
vocabulary.visual: Range 26 covers 68 to 94; IQR 12.5 covers only 75.5 to 88

vocabulary.definition: The distance from the least value to the greatest value, found by subtracting: greatest − least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia del valor menor al mayor, que se halla restando: mayor − menor.

vocabulary.definition: One of the three values that cut an ordered data set into four equal-sized groups.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los tres valores que dividen un conjunto ordenado de datos en cuatro grupos del mismo tamaño.

vocabulary.definition: The distance across the middle half of the data, found by subtracting the first quartile from the third: Q3 − Q1.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia a lo largo de la mitad central de los datos: se resta el primer cuartil del tercero: Q3 − Q1.
vocabulary.visual: 88 − 75.5 = 12.5 — the width of the box on a box plot

vocabulary.definition: How much the values in a data set differ from one another — whether they sit close together or far apart.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto se diferencian entre sí los valores de un conjunto de datos: si están juntos o muy separados.
vocabulary.visual: Close together = low variability; spread apart = high variability

vocabulary.definition: A single number that describes the spread of a whole data set. The range and the IQR are both measures of variation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que describe la dispersión de todo un conjunto de datos. El rango y el RIC son medidas de variación.
vocabulary.visual: One number stands in for the spread of all 20 scores

2-5.workedExample:
Here are 20 history test scores in order: 68, 70, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 80, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 86, 88, 88, 90, 90, 93, 94. Ordering them first is what makes every step after this possible.
Range: I subtract the least value from the greatest. 94 − 68 = 26. The scores span 26 points from end to end.
Now the quartiles. The median splits the 20 scores into two halves of 10. The median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values: (83 + 84) ÷ 2 = 83.5.
Q1 is the median of the lower 10 values: halfway between 75 and 76, so Q1 = 75.5. Q3 is the median of the upper 10: halfway between 88 and 88, so Q3 = 88.
Interquartile range: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 88 − 75.5 = 12.5. The middle half of the students' scores differed by only 12.5 points, even though the full range was 26.

2-6.title: Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm
2-6.contentObjective: I can divide multi-digit whole numbers and explain the meaning of the quotient and remainder.
2-6.languageObjective: I can explain my division using the words dividend, divisor, quotient, and remainder.

vocabulary.definition: Separate a multi-digit number into equal groups to find a quotient.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un número de varias cifras en grupos iguales para hallar un cociente.

vocabulary.definition: The number you are splitting up in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que estás repartiendo en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 156 ÷ 12 = 13, the dividend is 156 — it is the total being split up

vocabulary.definition: The number you split by in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número entre el que divides en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 156 ÷ 12 = 13, the divisor is 12 — it is the size of each group

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.
vocabulary.visual: In 156 ÷ 12 = 13, the quotient is 13 — there are 13 groups

vocabulary.definition: What is left over when a number does not divide evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que sobra cuando un número no se divide de forma exacta.
vocabulary.visual: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 R 2 means 3 groups of 5 with 2 left over

vocabulary.definition: A method that repeats four steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until there are no digits left to bring down.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un método que repite cuatro pasos — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — hasta que no quedan dígitos por bajar.
vocabulary.visual: 1,344 ÷ 12 → divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, repeat

vocabulary.definition: The fourth step of long division: move the next digit of the dividend down next to what is left, then start the cycle again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El cuarto paso de la división larga: baja el siguiente dígito del dividendo junto a lo que sobró y vuelve a empezar el ciclo.
vocabulary.visual: 13 − 12 = 1, then bring down the 4 to make 14

2-6.workedExample:
I want 1,344 ÷ 12. The dividend is 1,344 and the divisor is 12, so 12 goes outside the bracket and 1,344 goes inside.
DIVIDE: 12 does not fit into 1, so I look at 13. How many 12s fit into 13? One. I write 1 above the 3.
MULTIPLY: 1 × 12 = 12. I write 12 underneath the 13.
SUBTRACT: 13 − 12 = 1. That is what is left so far.
BRING DOWN: I bring the next digit, 4, down next to the 1 to make 14. Now I repeat the cycle.
REPEAT: 14 ÷ 12 → 1 (written above the 4), 1 × 12 = 12, 14 − 12 = 2, and I bring down the last 4 to make 24.
REPEAT: 24 ÷ 12 → 2 (written above the last 4), 2 × 12 = 24, 24 − 24 = 0. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 0.
The digits I wrote are 1, 1, 2, so 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112. I check by multiplying: 12 × 112 = 1,344.

2-7.title: Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm
2-7.contentObjective: I can divide with decimals by making the divisor a whole number first.
2-7.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words dividend, divisor, quotient, and equivalent division.

vocabulary.definition: Find a quotient with decimals by sliding both decimal points right until the divisor is a whole number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar un cociente con decimales deslizando ambos puntos decimales a la derecha hasta que el divisor sea un número entero.

vocabulary.definition: The number you are splitting up in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que estás repartiendo en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 8.4 ÷ 2.1 = 4, the dividend is 8.4 — it is the total being split

vocabulary.definition: The number you split by in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número entre el que divides en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 8.4 ÷ 2.1 = 4, the divisor is 2.1 — it is the size of each group

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you divide.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando divides.
vocabulary.visual: In 8.4 ÷ 2.1 = 4, the quotient is 4 — there are 4 groups

vocabulary.definition: Dividing with decimals. First move the point to make the number you divide by whole, then run the long-division cycle.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dividir con decimales. Primero mueve el punto para hacer entero el número entre el que divides y luego repite el ciclo de la división larga.

vocabulary.definition: Multiplying both numbers by 10 or 100 gives the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar ambos números por 10 o 100 da la misma respuesta.
vocabulary.visual: 7.56 ÷ 0.12 = 756 ÷ 12 = 63 (both multiplied by 100)

2-7.workedExample:
I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and long division needs a whole-number divisor.
STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor, so 6.3 becomes 63.
I slide the decimal point 1 place to the right in the dividend too, so 18.9 becomes 189. Both points slid the same 1 place, so the answer does not change. The problem is now 189 ÷ 63.
DIVIDE: 63 does not fit into 1 or 18, so my first working number is 189. How many 63s fit into 189? Three. I write 3 above the 9.
MULTIPLY: 3 × 63 = 189. I write it underneath.
SUBTRACT: 189 − 189 = 0.
BRING DOWN: there are no digits left to bring down, so the cycle is finished and the remainder is 0. 18.9 ÷ 6.3 = 3.
I check by multiplying: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correct — 3 pods can be filled.

2-8.title: Describe Data Using the Mean
2-8.contentObjective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.
2-8.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words mean, average, measure of center, balance point, and data set.

vocabulary.definition: The average of a data set. Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio de un conjunto de datos. Suma todos los valores y divide entre cuántos valores hay.
vocabulary.visual: Miguel earned $60 in 4 days: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so the mean is $15 per day.

vocabulary.definition: Another word for the mean — the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Otra palabra para la media: la cantidad que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: A player averages 15 points per game, so over 10 games she scores 15 × 10 = 150 points in all.

vocabulary.definition: A single number used to describe the middle, or typical value, of a whole data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que se usa para describir el centro, o valor típico, de todo un conjunto de datos.
vocabulary.visual: The mean, $15, is one measure of center that describes all four of Miguel's days at once.

vocabulary.definition: The value where the total distance of the data above it equals the total distance below it. The mean is the balance point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor donde la distancia total de los datos por encima es igual a la distancia total por debajo. La media es el punto de equilibrio.
vocabulary.visual: With a target mean of 15, points totaling 13 below must be matched by points totaling 13 above.

vocabulary.definition: The whole collection of values that were gathered or measured.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Toda la colección de valores que se recopilaron o midieron.
vocabulary.visual: Sofia's points in games 1–9 — 12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10, 18 — form one data set.

2-8.workedExample:
Miguel's 4 days of earnings are shown with counters. When I combine all of the counters, there are 60 of them, which means Miguel earned $60 in all.
Now I redistribute the 60 counters equally among the 4 days. Each of the 4 groups ends up with 15 counters.
The arithmetic does exactly the same thing: I find the total, 60, and divide it by the number of days, 4. So 60 ÷ 4 = 15.
We can use $15 to describe Miguel's typical daily earnings. That leveled value is the mean.

2-9.title: Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation
2-9.contentObjective: I can find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) to describe how spread out data is.
2-9.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words mean absolute deviation, deviation, absolute value, and spread.

vocabulary.definition: The average distance of data values from the mean; it describes spread.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia promedio de los valores de datos respecto a la media; describe la dispersión.
vocabulary.visual: MAD = sum of absolute distances from the mean ÷ number of values.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from the mean.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de la media.
vocabulary.visual: If mean = 20 and value = 17, deviation = 17 − 20 = −3 (3 below the mean)

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from zero. It is never negative.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de cero. Nunca es negativo.
vocabulary.visual: |−3| = 3 and |3| = 3 — both are 3 units from zero

vocabulary.definition: How far apart the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: Low spread: 8, 9, 10, 11 (close together). High spread: 2, 9, 10, 25 (far apart)

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: A set clustered tightly around the mean has low MAD; a set spread far from the mean has high MAD

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: Low variability (MAD = 1): very consistent. High variability (MAD = 8): very spread out

2-9.workedExample:
My data set: 6, 8, 10, 12. First I find the mean: 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 = 36, then 36 ÷ 4 = 9. The mean is 9.
Next I find each deviation (value − mean): 6−9 = −3, 8−9 = −1, 10−9 = 1, 12−9 = 3.
Then I take the absolute value of each (the distance, always positive): 3, 1, 1, 3.
Finally I average those distances: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8, then 8 ÷ 4 = 2. So the MAD = 2 points.

3-7.workedExample:
Evelyn sees a Canadian highway sign reading 100 kilometers per hour and wonders whether that is faster or slower than 100 miles per hour.

5-1.contentObjective: I can find the area of a parallelogram using base × height.
5-1.languageObjective: I can explain how I found the area using the words base, height, area, and formula.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un paralelogramo. Fórmula: A = b × h, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = b × h; if b = 10 cm and h = 6 cm, A = 60 cm².

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado que está inclinado en vez de subir y bajar verticalmente. No es la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: In a leaning parallelogram, use the dashed 90° height—not the slanted side—in A = b × h.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con dos pares de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: Think of a leaning door — the top and bottom are parallel, and the two sides are parallel, like a slanted rectangle

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a parallelogram can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un paralelogramo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.
vocabulary.visual: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height at 90° to that side in A = b × h

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta hacia arriba desde la base hasta la parte de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top side straight down to the base, forming a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A 3 cm × 4 cm rectangle covers 12 square centimeters — imagine 12 tiny 1×1 squares inside it

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.
vocabulary.visual: An L-shaped room = a 10×8 rectangle joined to a 4×5 rectangle; total area = 80 + 20 = 100 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.
vocabulary.visual: A = b × h means Area equals base times height; for a parallelogram with b = 6 and h = 4, A = 24

5-1.workedExample:
I have a parallelogram with a base of 14 feet and a height of 9 feet.
I write the formula: A = base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = 14 × 9.
I multiply: 14 × 9 = 126.
So the area is 126 square feet. I used the height of 9, not the slanted side.

5-2.title: Determine the Area of Triangles
5-2.contentObjective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.
5-2.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words base, height, area, and perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y altura, por eso A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h; if b = 8 and h = 5, then A = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 square units

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a triangle can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un triángulo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.
vocabulary.visual: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height from the opposite vertex at 90° to that side in A = ½ × b × h

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top point straight down to the base at a 90° angle — like dropping a plumb line

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A triangle with b = 8 and h = 6 has area = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 sq units — exactly half the rectangle around it

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se unen formando una esquina recta (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The corner of a book or a door frame — the edges meet at exactly 90°, shown by a small square symbol

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.
vocabulary.visual: A house shape = a rectangle (the walls) + a triangle (the roof); total area = rectangle area + triangle area

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h means Area equals one-half times base times height; for b = 12 and h = 8, A = 48

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

5-2.workedExample:
My triangular garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I multiply base × height first: 12 × 8 = 96.
I take half: ½ × 96 = 48. So the area is 48 square feet.

5-3.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words trapezoid, base, height, and area.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a trapezoid. Formula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un trapecio. Fórmula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.visual: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with just one pair of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con solo un par de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: A table top wider than the bottom shelf — the top and bottom edges are parallel, the two sides slant inward

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los dos lados paralelos de un trapecio.
vocabulary.visual: If the bottom of the trapezoid is 10 ft, then b₁ = 10 ft in the formula A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h

vocabulary.definition: The other parallel side of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El otro lado paralelo de un trapecio.
vocabulary.visual: If the top of the trapezoid is 6 ft, then b₂ = 6 ft; both bases are parallel to each other

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance between the two parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta entre los dos lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top base straight down to the bottom base at a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A trapezoid with b₁ = 10, b₂ = 6, h = 4 has area = ½(10 + 6) × 4 = 32 sq units

5-3.workedExample:
My trapezoid window has a top base of 4 feet, a bottom base of 8 feet, and a height of 5 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
I add the bases first: 4 + 8 = 12.
I multiply by the height: 12 × 5 = 60.
I take half: ½ × 60 = 30. So the area is 30 square feet.

5-4.title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
5-4.contentObjective: I can find the area of a composite figure by adding or subtracting the areas of basic shapes.
5-4.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words composite figure, decompose, add, and subtract.

vocabulary.definition: The total space inside a figure made of basic shapes. Formula: A = A₁ + A₂ — add the parts (or subtract a missing piece).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio total dentro de una figura formada por figuras básicas. Fórmula: A = A₁ + A₂ — suma las partes (o resta la pieza que falta).
vocabulary.visual: Total area = area of rectangle 1 + area of rectangle 2.

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.
vocabulary.visual: An L-shaped room = a 12×8 rectangle joined to a 6×5 rectangle; total area = 96 + 30 = 126 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: To break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar una figura en figuras más pequeñas y simples.
vocabulary.visual: Draw a dashed line across the L-shape to split it into two rectangles — now you can find each area separately

vocabulary.definition: Add up the areas of the smaller shapes to get the total.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar las áreas de las figuras pequeñas para obtener el total.
vocabulary.visual: T-shaped hallway: top rectangle = 30 sq ft, bottom rectangle = 28 sq ft → total = 30 + 28 = 58 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: Take away the area of a missing piece from a bigger shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Quitar el área de una parte que falta de una figura más grande.
vocabulary.visual: A 14×10 pool with a 6×4 cutout: 140 − 24 = 116 sq ft of water surface

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.
vocabulary.visual: Rectangle: A = l × w; Triangle: A = ½ × b × h; use the right formula for each piece of a composite figure

5-4.workedExample:
My L-shaped room splits into two rectangles: one is 12 ft by 8 ft, the other is 6 ft by 5 ft.
First rectangle: A = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 square feet.
Second rectangle: A = 6 × 5 = 30 square feet.
The pieces are joined, so I add: 96 + 30 = 126.
So the total area is 126 square feet.

5-5.contentObjective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges using length × width × height.

vocabulary.termEs: Volumen con aristas de números enteros
vocabulary.definition: The number of unit cubes inside a rectangular prism. Formula: V = l × w × h.

vocabulary.visual: V = l × w × h; 3 × 4 × 5 = 60 cubic units.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura sólida.
vocabulary.visual: A box 3 × 2 × 4 holds 24 unit cubes, so V = 24 cubic units

vocabulary.definition: A solid box shape with six flat rectangle sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura sólida en forma de caja con seis lados rectangulares.
vocabulary.visual: A cereal box or shoe box — it has length, width, and height

vocabulary.definition: The units used to measure space inside, like cubic inches.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las unidades para medir el espacio interior, como pulgadas cúbicas.
vocabulary.visual: A tiny cube that is 1 in × 1 in × 1 in = 1 in³ (one cubic inch)

vocabulary.definition: How long, how wide, and how tall a box is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan largo, ancho y alto es una caja.
vocabulary.visual: V = l × w × h: for a box 5 × 3 × 2, volume = 30 cubic units

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape that folds up into a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana que se dobla y forma un sólido.
vocabulary.visual: A cross-shaped pattern of 6 rectangles folds into a rectangular box

vocabulary.definition: The line where two flat sides of a solid meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea donde se unen dos lados planos de un sólido.
vocabulary.visual: A cube has 12 edges — 4 along the top, 4 along the bottom, 4 vertical

5-5.workedExample:
My time capsule box is 6 long, 4 wide, and 3 tall. I write the formula: V = length × width × height.
I put in the numbers: V = 6 × 4 × 3.
First I multiply two of them: 6 × 4 = 24.
Then I multiply by the last one: 24 × 3 = 72.
So the volume is 72 cubic units. I use cubic units because volume fills space in 3 directions.

5-6.contentObjective: I can find the surface area of a solid by using its net.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of all the flat sides of a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El área total de todos los lados planos de un sólido.
vocabulary.visual: A box 6 × 4 × 2: SA = 2(24) + 2(12) + 2(8) = 88 in² — like wrapping paper needed

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape that folds up into a solid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana que se dobla y forma un sólido.
vocabulary.visual: Cut along the edges of a cereal box and unfold it flat — you see all 6 faces

vocabulary.definition: One flat side of a solid shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado plano de una figura sólida.
vocabulary.visual: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right

vocabulary.definition: A flat shape with length and width, but no thickness.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura plana con largo y ancho, pero sin grosor.
vocabulary.visual: A rectangle drawn on paper is 2D — it has length and width but no depth

vocabulary.definition: The line where two flat sides of a solid meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea donde se unen dos lados planos de un sólido.
vocabulary.visual: A cube has 12 edges — the lines where two flat faces connect

5-6.workedExample:
My box is 8 in. long, 5 in. wide, and 3 in. tall. I unfold it into a net and see 3 pairs of faces.
Top and bottom: each is 8 × 5 = 40, and there are 2 of them, so 2 × 40 = 80.
Front and back: each is 8 × 3 = 24, so 2 × 24 = 48.
Left and right: each is 5 × 3 = 15, so 2 × 15 = 30.
I add all the pairs: 80 + 48 + 30 = 158. The surface area is 158 in².

vocabulary.definition: A toothed wheel that passes motion to another toothed wheel through a chain.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of two quantities, like pedal rotations to wheel rotations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de dos cantidades, como rotaciones del pedal y rotaciones de la rueda.
vocabulary.visual: 48 pedal teeth to 12 wheel teeth — 4 wheel turns for every pedal turn.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that make the same comparison using different numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que hacen la misma comparación con números diferentes.
vocabulary.visual: 1 : 4 and 3 : 12 describe the same gear, at different sizes.

10-4.workedExample:
A later bicycle design uses a chain: the pedal gear has 48 teeth, and the largest rear gear has 32 teeth.
For each rotation of the 48-tooth pedal gear, the wheel gear also turns 48 teeth.
The 32-tooth gear needs to turn 32 teeth to make one full rotation, so I find the equivalent ratio: 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5.
The rear wheel makes 1.5 rotations for each pedal rotation — this gear makes it easier to pedal at slower speeds or go uphill.

10-5.title: Math is Boundless
10-5.contentObjective: I can create and describe geometric designs using repetition, patterns, and rhythm, and use a pattern unit to predict what comes next.
10-5.languageObjective: I can describe a design using the words repetition, pattern, pattern unit, and rhythm.

vocabulary.definition: The same object, shape, or form repeated multiple times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mismo objeto, figura o forma repetido varias veces.
vocabulary.visual: The same tile, over and over, all the way along the border.

vocabulary.definition: A set of objects or shapes that are repeated and arranged in a regular order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de objetos o figuras que se repiten y se organizan en un orden regular.
vocabulary.visual: Circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle …

vocabulary.definition: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La parte más pequeña de un patrón que se repite.
vocabulary.visual: circle · square · triangle — the chunk that starts over.

vocabulary.definition: A design element created by varying the placement, size, orientation, or order of the same objects or shapes.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un elemento de diseño creado al variar la posición, el tamaño, la orientación o el orden de los mismos objetos o figuras.
vocabulary.visual: The same circles, but sizes and spacing change as your eye travels.

vocabulary.definition: Being able to know what comes next because the design follows a rule.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Poder saber qué viene después porque el diseño sigue una regla.
vocabulary.visual: Shape 25 must be a circle — the unit repeats every 3.

10-5.workedExample:
A border repeats: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, ...
The pattern unit is 3 shapes long: circle, square, triangle.
To predict shape number 12, I divide: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — it is the blue triangle.
The next three shapes after any complete unit will be a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.

10-6.title: Math is Mine
10-6.contentObjective: I can look back at my answers from Lesson 1-1, describe how my math biography has changed this year, and recognize ways we are all doers of math.
10-6.languageObjective: I can compare my beginning-of-year and end-of-year math stories using the words then, now, changed, and grown.

vocabulary.definition: The story of your relationship with math — and how it has changed over time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La historia de tu relación con las matemáticas y cómo ha cambiado con el tiempo.
vocabulary.visual: September: “I am not a math person.” June: “I can explain why it works.”

vocabulary.definition: To look back at what you did, felt, and learned, and think about what it means.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar atrás a lo que hiciste, sentiste y aprendiste, y pensar en lo que significa.
vocabulary.visual: Looking back at the tram problem: what worked, what you would change.

vocabulary.definition: The change between what you could do before and what you can do now.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El cambio entre lo que podías hacer antes y lo que puedes hacer ahora.
vocabulary.visual: In Unit 1 you estimated 80 riders; now you find 480 riders per hour.

vocabulary.definition: Trusting yourself to try a problem, even when the first attempt might fail.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Confiar en ti mismo para intentar un problema, aunque el primer intento pueda fallar.
vocabulary.visual: Starting a hard problem before you are sure it will work.

vocabulary.definition: The people and places around you — where math shows up outside the classroom.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las personas y los lugares que te rodean, donde las matemáticas aparecen fuera del aula.
vocabulary.visual: The people and places where math shows up — home, work, the neighborhood.

10-6.workedExample:
In September I estimated the Ferris wheel: 20 cars with about 4 riders each is 20 × 4 = 80 riders — 'about 80.'
Now I can go further with this year's math: at 6 turns an hour, that wheel moves about 80 × 6 = 480 riders per hour.
Same wheel, same me — but my toolbox grew. That difference IS my math story.
